_comment: Raw INPUT_TYPES harvested from a real ComfyUI install by scripts/harvest-comfy-node-defs.py. Input ORDER is what scripts/adapt-workflow.js needs: the UI format stores widget values positionally and only names the ones that are linked.

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Bit depth of the created video. 10-bit keeps smoother gradients with less banding, but some players and downstream nodes may not support it.

vae.tooltip: The VAE model used for decoding the latent.

model.tooltip: Model to attach the preview override to.

max_resolution.tooltip: Max preview side in pixels for the live widget. 0 = full sampler resolution (no downscale).

jpeg_quality.tooltip: JPEG quality for the live preview transport.

suppress_default_preview.tooltip: Suppress the standard sampler-node preview overlay while sampling, so only this node's frame updates. Progress bar still advances normally.

preview_frames.tooltip: Frames to sample from each video step's latent for animated preview. 1 = single frame (current behavior, fastest). >1 = animated WebP playing back at preview_fps. Only applies to video models (5D latents); ignored for image models.

preview_fps.tooltip: Playback FPS for the animated WebP preview. Ignored when preview_frames=1.

vae.tooltip: Optional LTX VAE for true-RGB previews. TAEHV-LTX = fast tiny decode (VAE pinned to GPU). Any other LTX VAE = full-quality decode via vae.decode() — MUCH slower per step.

tiny_vae.tooltip: Tiny VAE decoder from models/vae_approx for true-RGB previews. Overrides Latent2RGB and the 'vae' input.

tau_start.tooltip: tau on the first, highest-noise step. Higher = more blocks take the approximate path = faster, lower fidelity.

tau_end.tooltip: tau on the final, low-noise steps where detail forms. Lower = denser attention at the end of sampling.

curve.tooltip: How tau interpolates between tau_start and tau_end across sampling. step switches at the midpoint.

min_tokens.tooltip: Use the stock attention forward below this packed sequence length.

strict.tooltip: Raise kernel errors instead of falling back. Enable while validating a new GPU or Triton version.

dense_percent.tooltip: Keep the stock dense attention for this fraction of early sampling (the Sol-Attn paper's recipe: 0.2). 0 disables the gate.

thresh_type.tooltip: Routing threshold estimator. diag is the evaluated default; exact uses second-moment statistics for more precise routing at extra precompute cost.

int8_qk.tooltip: Quantize q/k to int8 for the exact attention path. Faster above ~16K tokens (measured 1.2-1.3x) at ~1% extra numerical error; slightly slower at 8K.

int8_pv.tooltip: Also quantize the P*V dot to int8 (per-token P, per-channel V). More speed on top of int8_qk at additional accuracy cost. Requires int8_qk. Opt-in.

sink_conditioning.tooltip: Keep H3's packed text/conditioning/reference/audio KV blocks exact (~3% cost, protects prompt adherence and audio sync). exact_kv_and_rows also runs those query rows dense (~20% cost). off disables the sink.

dense_blocks.tooltip: Transformer blocks to keep dense, e.g. '0-2,-1' for the first three and the last. Negative indices count from the end. First and last blocks are the most approximation-sensitive. Empty sparsifies all.

resize_type.tooltip: Choose to scale by a multiplier or to exact target dimensions.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: The aspect ratio for the output dimensions.

megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels. 1.0 MP ≈ 1024x1024 for square.

multiple.tooltip: Nearest multiple of the result to set the selected resolution to.

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, snapped up to the model's 17k+5 grid (124 = ~5s; trained range is ~124-362, longer is untested)

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the file to save. This may include formatting information such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width% to include values from nodes.

format.tooltip: The format to save the video as.

codec.tooltip: The codec to use for the video.

encoding.tooltip: Automatic preserves compatible H.264 streams. Re-encode applies a custom CRF.

crf.tooltip: Lower values produce higher quality and larger files.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

lora_name: SDXL\8.0-sprite pixel art style by skormino.safetensors

mirostat.tooltip: Whether to use Mirostat sampling. Mirostat is an algorithm that actively maintains the quality of generated text within a desired range during text generation. (0 = disabled, 1 = Mirostat 1, 2 = Mirostat 2.0)

mirostat_eta.tooltip: Mirostat's learning rate parameter influences how quickly the algorithm responds to feedback from the generated text.

mirostat_tau.tooltip: Mirostat's target entropy parameter controls the balance between coherence and diversity in the generated text.

num_ctx.tooltip: Sets the size of the context window used to generate the next token.

repeat_last_n.tooltip: Sets how far back for the model to look back to prevent repetition. (0 = disabled, -1 = num_ctx)

repeat_penalty.tooltip: Sets how strongly to penalize repetitions. A higher value (e.g., 1.5) will penalize repetitions more strongly, while a lower value (e.g., 0.9) will be more lenient.

temperature.tooltip: Increasing the temperature will make the model answer more creatively.

seed.tooltip: Sets the random number seed to use for generation. Setting this to a specific number will make the model generate the same text for the same prompt.

stop.tooltip: When this pattern is encountered the LLM will stop generating text and return.

num_predict.tooltip: Maximum number of tokens to predict when generating text. The default -1 means infinite generation.

top_k.tooltip: Reduces the probability of generating nonsense. A higher value (e.g. 100) will give more diverse answers, while a lower value (e.g. 10) will be more conservative.

top_p.tooltip: Works together with top-k. A higher value (e.g., 0.95) will lead to more diverse text, while a lower value (e.g., 0.5) will generate more focused and conservative text.

min_p.tooltip: Alternative to the top_p, and aims to ensure a balance of quality and variety. The parameter p represents the minimum probability for a token to be considered, relative to the probability of the most likely token. For example, with p=0.05 and the most likely token having a probability of 0.9, logits with a value less than 0.045 are filtered out.

debug.tooltip: For debugging purposes of the custom nodes, no effect on ollama api.

url.tooltip: The URL of the Ollama server. Default value points to a local instance with ollama's default port configuration.

model.tooltip: Select a model for inference. This is a list of available models on the Ollama server. If you don't see any, make sure the Ollama server is running on the url and there are models installed.

keep_alive.tooltip: Configures how long ollama keeps the model loaded in memory after inference. -1 = keep alive indefinitely, 0 = unload model immediately after inference

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

filename_prefix.tooltip: The prefix for the file to save. This may include formatting information such as %date:yyyy-MM-dd% or %Empty Latent Image.width% to include values from nodes.

model_format.tooltip:
VAE latent configuration:
• SDXL (not compatible with SD 1.5)
• Flux (Flux, Z-Image Turbo, Lumina)
• Flux2 (Flux2, Flux2 Klein: BN-packed latent)
• Ideogram 4 (Flux2: shift/scale-packed latent)
• Wan 2.1 (Wan 2.x, Krea 2, Anima, Qwen Image)

width.tooltip: The width of the latent images in pixels.

height.tooltip: The height of the latent images in pixels.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent images in the batch.

system.tooltip: System prompt - use this to set the role and general behavior of the model.

prompt.tooltip: User prompt - a question or task you want the model to answer or perform. For vision tasks, you can refer to the input image as 'this image', 'photo' etc. like 'Describe this image in detail'

think.tooltip: If enabled, the model will do a thinking process before answering. This can result in more accurate results. The thinking is then available as a separate output for debugging or understanding how the model arrived at its answer. Some models don't support this feature and the generation will fail.

keep_context.tooltip: If enabled, the model will keep the context of the conversation and use it for the next generation. This is useful for multi-turn conversations or tasks that require context.

format.tooltip: Output format of the response. 'text' will return a plain text response, while 'json' will return a structured response in JSON format. This is useful when the model is part of a larger pipeline and you need additional processing on the response. In this case I recommend showing the model example outputs in the system prompt. Some models are not trained to perform well in structured output.

connectivity.tooltip: Set an ollama provider for the generation. If this input is empty, the 'meta' input must be set.

options.tooltip: Connect an Ollama Options node for advanced inference configuration.

images.tooltip: Provide an image or a batch of images for vision tasks. Make sure that the selected model supports vision, otherwise it may hallucinate the response.

context.tooltip: Optionally set an existing model context, useful for multi-turn conversations, follow-up questions.

meta.tooltip: Use this input to chain multiple 'Ollama Generate' nodes. In this case the connectivity and options inputs are passed along.
